notes.text: Rav Huna is the one who entered. The sukkah belongs to Rabbi Yochanan, the scribe of Gufta. Render the direction explicitly from the named source.
The Yerushalmi gives Chanin of Guftayya speaking to Shmuel about Rav Chiyya bar Ashi. Preserve Heilprin’s Chanan of Gufta as his received wording.
The checked digital edition has the quoted observation at 3:7:2. It identifies Yonatan as the scribe of Gufta and Bar Avuna as the scribe who read the Song of the Well. Preserve the received 3:8.
The Soferim parallel gives Rabbi Yonatan, the scribe of Guftera, and Rabbi Avuna the scribe. These forms remain distinct from the Megillah formulation.
The internal pointer leads to the entry for Yitzchak bar Gufta. The entry supplies separate reports involving Rabbi Mana.
Keep Yochanan, Chanan or Chanin, Yonatan and Yitzchak attributed to the respective notices. Shared place and occupation do not settle identity.
